wines.title: Adega Algueira 'Escalada'
wines.header: Adega Algueira 'Escalada' , Godello, Ribeira Sacra, Spain, 2024
description: A wine which clearly shows the massive potential of Godello as a variety. Fermented in old oak and chestnut barrels but matured in stainless, this is layered and complex, with everything from Orange bloom, peach and apricot to honey, almond and fennel. wines.header: Alexis Pollier 'Le Clos' Macon-Milly Lamartine, Chardonnay, France, 2023
description: 100% Chardonnay

A zippy example of a chardonnay from the Macon region, framed biodynamically Alexis Pollier produces fruit focused styles of white burgundy. wines.title: Alta Alella 'Exeo' Cava De Paraje
wines.header: Alta Alella 'Exeo' Cava De Paraje, Spain, 2016
description: Grape: 60% Pansa Blanca and 40% Chardonnay

Cava de Paraje Calificado is Cava’s newest and highest classification and is the equivalent to a Grand Cru -it is only awarded to the finest wines from the very best sites. The wines of Alta Alella display finesse and complexity to rival- and even surpass- many top-end Champagnes.The Mirgin Exeo comes from the Paratge Vallcirera-Serra de Mar, which is where Alta Alella lies. The soils are Sailó, so acidic, rough granite sand. Produced only in exceptional years the Exeo is macerated and fermented in 2 and 3 year old barrels and is then aged for over 5 years before being released. There’s a nice level of toasty aromas plus floral and ripe fruits. It’s creamy with distinct minerality, balanced with the ripe fruits and toast flavors. This is an excellent example of Cava.

“Remarkably powerful, lots of aromas and flavors. The oak is perfectly integrated. On the nose, it has some toasty note I don’t find in the palate. Dry style, I like the mellow texture and the finesse of the mousse. Quite ample with brioche and creamy aftertaste. Very complete and delightful wine. A great vintage!” Janis Robinson.com
An exceptional aperitif, delicious with smoked salmon, prawns, a plate of oysters or roast chicken.

wines.title: Alta Alella 'Mirgin Opus' Cava De Paraje
wines.header: Alta Alella 'Mirgin Opus' Cava De Paraje, Spain, 2019
description: Grape: 60% Chardonnay and 40% Pansa Blanca
Cava de Paraje Calificado is Cava’s newest and highest classification and is the equivalent to a Grand Cru -it is awarded to the finest wines from the very best sites.

The Mirgin Opus comes from the Paratge Vallcirera-Serra de Mar, which is where Alta Alella lies. The soils are Sailó, so acidic, rough granite sand. The Chardonnay is fermented in two year old French oak barrels, while the Pansa Blanca is fermented in stainless steel. 2019 was an excellent year with very healthy grapes giving ripe white fruits and flowers on the nose, with seaside salinity. The white fruits follows through, some nut flavors. Lovely, balanced, acidity and a depth and long length, from the 3 years of aging, makes for a world class sparkling wine.
Brilliant as an aperitif and delicious with seafood or a roast chicken sandwich!

wines.title: Alta Alella PB
wines.header: Alta Alella PB, Spain, 2024
description: Grape: Pansa Blanca

This is the perfect all rounder! The Alta Alella PB is wonderfully light, has very generous fruit quality due to the high quality grapes which are organically grown. Once it opens up, this wine shows amazing character, great minerality, fresh tropical fruits, notes of green almonds. Great if you're into Chablis or Alberino and want to try something a little different and easy. This is the one!
wines.pairing: seafood and light chicken dishes

wines.title: Alta Alella TALLAROL
wines.header: Alta Alella TALLAROL, Spain, 2019
description: Grape: Pansa Blanca

A fantastic Spanish white made from Pansa Blanca also known as Xarel·lo. With aromas of white fruit (pear and apple), green almonds and hints of fennel and citrus on the nose. wines.title: Arpepe 'Il Pettirosso' 2023 Valtellina Superiore DOCG
wines.header: Arpepe 'Il Pettirosso' Valtellina Superiore DOCG, Italy 2023
description: The 2023 Il Pettitrosso comes from the winery's top sites, Sassella, Inferno and Grumello, and is a seriously good introduction to the wines of Arpepe and indeed to the beguiling elegance of 'Alpine Nebbiolo' of Valtellina. The 2023 vintage was wamer, giving a more structured and richer Il Pettirosso than previous releases.

The grapes spend up to 3 months on their skins and another 12 in used oak barrels, giving the wine certain dusty, dry tannins. There's red berry fruits, raspberries, strawberries, and cherries hiding behind the tea-like tannins that reveal themselves gently in the glass. Although this is a lighter, more delicate style of Nebbiolo there's so much going on it the glass and, as with all of Arpepe's wines, your patience once you've opened the bottle will reward you in spades!

wines.title: Arpepe 'Rocce Rosse' 2016 Sassella Valtellina Sassella Superiore Riserva
wines.header: Arpepe 'Rocce Rosse' Valtellina Superiore Sassella Riserva, Italy 2016
description: Named after the iron-rich 'red rock' of this cru-subzone, the Rocce Rosse is only made in exceptional vintages. It's a more powerful, dense wine (by Arpepe standards). Like most of their wines, this is beguiling, with smoke, dark spice, lavender and star anise on the nose. There's a richness and structure that reflects the granite terraces, the hard working vines, the 40 day maceration and 5 years of aging in barrel, concrete vats and eventually bottles. A triumph.

"Very flowery on the nose, with fresh violets, roses, red currants, bright fruitiness, licorice and stony minerality. The attack is soft, with a medium body, brilliant crisp acidity and tight yet ripe tannins soaked in fruit. Not an easy wine, more elegant than powerful. It needs time to develop more complexity. Drinkable now, but best from 2026." 96 JamesSuckling.com Aug 2024

"The Ar. Pe. Pe. 2016 Valtellina Superiore Riserva Sassella Rocce Rosse is initially understated with timid primary fruit, blood orange and apricot. There is a pretty spiciness as well, with dried cinnamon stick, nutmeg and tanned leather. The wine needs time, and if you come back to the glass after a little pause, it sings with greater intensity and balance. This is a release of 25,302 bottles that sees 97 days on the skins and 34 months of wood and cement aging." 96 Wine Advocate Jan 2024
This is an exceptional wine, a heroic wine and one worthy of any cellar or, more importantly, any moment that should be shared and cherished, with yourself or with a worthy friend. Enjoy.

quote.text: Tight, taut and very young, this gorgeous wine has intense aromas of Alpine berry, orange zest, camphor and cake spice. On the savory, elegantly structured palate, firm tannins accompany crushed mint, wild strawberry, pomegranate and grilled Porcini. A salty note signals the close while vibrant acidity keeps it balanced." Drink through 2046 98 Kerin O'Keefe December 2024

description: From 50-100-year-old vines in the Buon Consiglio and San Antonio single vineyards in the Grumello subzone of Valtellina, lying beneath the fourteenth century Castel Gremello that lends its' name to the wine. There's a little more subsoil here and that gives the wine a certain softness over its siblings, Sassella and Inferno, making them a little more accessible sooner.

"The 2016 Valtellina Superiore Grumello Riserva Sant’Antonio is now fully mature. Dried cherry, cedar, pipe tobacco, mint, dried herbs and brown spice are all consistent with a wine that is peaking today. The 2016 has enough energy to drink well for another handful years, but I would not push my luck too far beyond that." 92 Vinous Feb 2026

"Dense and layered, this opens nicely with air in the glass, revealing flavors of dried raspberry, eucalyptus, leather and black tea enmeshed with a core of firm tannins. Showing fine balance and good energy overall, this should shine even brighter after short-term cellaring." 94 Wine Spectator March 2024

quote.text: Game, smoke, earth, strawberries and bright licorice root depth. The attack is soft and elegant, with silky tannins and refreshing acidity. A chewy, vivid finish." 93 JamesSuckling.com June 2024

wines.header: ArPePe 'Stella Retica' Valtellina Superiore Sassella, Italy 2017

Sassella translates as Rock in the local dialect. With long macerations, 50 days on its' skins and the incredible terroir, gives this wine a remarkable minerality.

wines.title: Arpepe 'Ultimi Raggi' 2016 Sassella Valtellina Sassella Superiore Riserva
wines.header: Arpepe 'Ultimi Raggi' Valtellina Superiore Sassella Riserva, Italy 2016
description: The Ultimi Raggi (meaning Last Rays) is a late-harvested Nebbiolo where the grapes undergo a light and natural drying process, due to the Alpine winds, while still attached to the vines. The later harvesting, before the snows in mind November, thickens the skins and concentrates the sugars, creating the most full-bodied and structured offering in the winery’s line-up. It has a naturally high acidity that comes, in part, from the plots 600 meter altitude, right up at the highest reaches of the Sassella subzone, in an area called Ere. Think Morello cherries, prunes and licorice, accompanied by firm, close-grained tannins that grip through to a long, beguiling finish.

"A lively, graceful red, well-spiced and aromatic, with a skein of incense and potpourri notes winding through cherry and berry fruit flavors. Reveals a savory push of loamy earth, mineral and brambly herbs on the plush finish." 92 Wine Spectator March 2024

wines.title: Arpepe 2024 Rosso Di Valtellina
wines.header: Arpepe Rosso Di Valtellina, Italy, 2024
description: A Nebbiolo that drinks like a Pinot. Light ruby colour, soft and fragrant on the nose -there’s that characteristic Nebbiolo hint of rose- red berry fruits, grippy tannins and a sprinkle of mountain magic, leading to a wonderfully silky finish. Oh So Good.

Although this is a lighter, more delicate style of Nebbiolo there's so much going on it the glass and, as with all of Arpepe's wines, your patience once you've opened the bottle will reward you in spades!
More on Arpepe

Nebbiolo from the Alps, from Valtellina in Lombardy to be exact, practically in Switzerland, where the wines are in every respect lighter and leaner than their better known Nebbiolo cousins in Barolo and Barbaresco or even northern Piedmont. They have their own set of aromas, wild berries, dried raspberries, flint, crushed granite and smoke, with a lively, focused purity from light, mineral infused grapes, some say they’re Pinot-esque. This is down to the poverty of the soil, essentially schist and granite, and the elevation of up to 700 meters above sea level resulting in fruit with intense minerality. The valley runs from Lake Como to the Stelvio Pass, west to east, with all the vineyards planted on the northern slopes with long sunshine days and a mild microclimate that’s almost Mediterranean like.
Located on impressively steep granite terraces which can be traced back to pre-Roman times, now a Unesco World Heritage site, the Perego family have been making wine here since 1860.

What distinguishes the wines of Ar.Pe.Pe. is their focus on long aging and tradition. Everything is worked by hand, with minimum intervention, and the wines only released when the family deem they’re ready for drinking. The wines though have the quality and depth to age gracefully.

There are plots in three specific sites in Sassella, Grumello and Inferno and they decide on the number of wines to vinify with each vintage. Meaning that, from year to year, the range can be quite different but always Nebbiolo and always with incredible results.

Each year they bottle a Rosso di Valtellina, a blend from any of the three sites. In the good vintages ARPEPE makes Valtellina Superiore wines from the Sassella, Grumello and Inferno, that see a longer maceration and up to 30 months in Chestnut barrels followed by time in bottle before being released. In exceptional vintages ARPEPE produces its five “Riserva” wines, wines that deserve both time and attention. Wines that appear pale and light but with a burgundy like elegance, delicate yet full, gentle and ethereal. Age-worthy and a must for any genuine cellar.

The results are graceful, fragrant reds that are naturally lighter on their feet and have lower alcohol levels than Barolo and Barbaresco but that feature depth, finesse and serious longevity. They also deliver their varietal pedigree, offering enticing sensations of rose, red berry, camphor and new leather as well as Alpine herb sensations, bright acidity, taut but refined tannins and savory mineral notes." Kerin O'Keefe www.kerinokeefe.com/arpepe/

quote.text: Valtellina Cradled among soaring Alpine peaks near the town of Sondrio in Italy’s northern Lombardy region, Valtellina’s steep mountain vineyards have been turning out notable wines for millennia. Nebbiolo has the starring role on the breathtakingly vertiginous slopes and currently accounts for 90% of Valtellina’s 850ha under vine. Planted predominantly in terraced, dry stone wall vineyards, Nebbiolo thrives in the area’s unique growing conditions. These include high altitude vineyards that are protected from strong winds and fierce storms by the Rhaetian Alps. The grape further benefits from mild breezes from Lake Como below and southern exposures that all together add up to a long growing season that generates aromatic complexity while rocky soils impart elegance and mineral sensations.

wines.header: Art Laietá  Mirgin Laietà Rosé 2020 Gran Reserva, Brut Nature
description: Grape: Mataró (Monastrell)

An organic Gran Reserva Rose from the Cava maestros Alta Alella. Made from the Matro (Monastrell) grape, the wine is aged in bottle for 30 months, giving it a lovely depth of flavour and silky bubbles. Elegant and stylish, and that’s not just the bottle, with soft red fruits, classic toastiness, minerally and saline with a wonderful long finish.
Beautifully presented in a Gift tube.

wines.header: Art Laietá Mirgin Cava Reserva, Alella, Spain, 2022
description: An exceptional Cava producer that tends to get less attention than some of the showier estates, but we like it that way. Crisp green apple, peach, and lemon fruit, fine bubbles, and great length. Properly dry.

This zero-dosage sparkling wine comes off a southeast-facing plot on the local sauló soil. After a gentle pressing, the base wine is fermented in stainless steel tanks. Once blended and bottled, it’s aged on the fine lees for 15 to 30 months prior to disgorgement

wines.title: Art Laietá ‘Laieta’ Gran Reserva Brut Nature Cava
wines.header: Art Laietá ‘Laieta’ Gran Reserva Brut Nature Cava, Alella, Barcellona, Spain, 2021
description: Grape: Panca Blanca (Xarel lo), Chardonnay, Pinot Noir

Set in the Serralada de Marina nature reserve, with the Mediterranean a kilometre or so below it and Barcellona clearly visible just beyond the hills, this winery sits among the vines in a small, natural amphitheatre. It’s also the family home of the Pujol-Busquets Guillen family. Today Mireia is the wine maker and she continues to herald the families dedication to conservation and organic practices. The family has also been at the forefront of elevating the quality and global recognition of Cava and they have helped create the classification systems that recognise single vineyards through the Paraje Calificado appellation and the Integral Producer stamp that ensures that the wines are 100% estate produced.

The Laieta Gran Reserva is simply delicious. It’s a wine of considerable quality, one that is complex and one that deserves to stand above many of its international peers. There’s green apple, peach and honey suckle on the nose. It’s dry with white stone fruits notes of peach and nectarine and a salinity that comes from the fine granite soils. The bubbles are elegant and persistent.
wines.pairing: almonds, Iberico ham, hard cheese, smoked salmon or cured trout

wines.title: As Caborcas 2020, Ladeiras do Biei, Valdeorras, Spain
wines.header: As Caborcas 2020 Ladeiras do Biei, Valdeorras, Spain
description: As Caborcas means 'vineyard by the little river' and this prized plot sits just above the Bibei river, outside the town of Santa Cruz. Having long been recognised by the older generation of local growers as being a special site, the team of Telmo Rodriguez started bottling this single vineyard wine in 2010. It's a field blend of organic Mencía, Merenzao, Sousón, Brancellao, Godello and more, from a complete mixture of altitudes and aspects. There's minimum intervention with wild yeast fermentation in small oak barrels and stainless steel tanks. Followed by up to 15 months in large foudres. As Caborcas tends to be intensely aromatic with silky, smooth tannins, it's complex, elegant yet powerful.

"The expressive, floral and aromatic 2020 As Caborcas was cropped from a warmer year but without the frost or mildew of past years like 2017 and 2018. 2020 was a year when they achieved a wine with good structure and a little more alcohol (14%) that was not really noticeable, as the wine comes through as balanced and elegant, textured and juicy, with fine tannins but not lacking clout." 2,664 bottles were produced. Robert Parker 96/100

"The nose is amazing. Sweet licorice with sweet sloe. A high intensity play of sweetness and acidity. Almost black forest raspberry underneath. Something like a highly ripe Cabernet Franc on the nose. Light strawberry comes behind it and garrigue spice, but all remains sweet. Sweet black cherry and a bit of amarena. The wine is not fat at all, it is infinitely fine on the nose. But highly aromatic, sweet, dense and rich. This charming fruit brings tears of joy to your eyes. What a brilliant composition! In the mouth, sweet black cherry with some charcoal. Underpinned with licorice, concentrated, almost blackish raspberry. Wonderful acidity and freshness, an acidity of red currant but more still of sweet cassis. The phenomenal thing about this wine is the play of sweetness and acidity. The oscillograph is enormous and at the same time it has this infinite charm from the high ripeness of the vintage. Highly ripe, high acidity and at the same time remaining lean and delicate. So brutally intense in the mouth! Concentrated finesse... Nothing heavy, but just standing for minutes with a brilliant charm factor - with a salty touch from the granite soils. A treat of the very highest order!" Heiner Lobenberg 97-100/100

To many, Telmo Rodriguez, who, along with his sister Amaia, runs the impressive Remelluri winery in Rioja, needs no introduction but it's his partnership with fellow winemaker, Pablo Egnziza that has created the exciting range of wines that come together under the umbrella of Telmo Rodriguez Wines. The two have have spent the past thirty years reclaiming abandoned vineyards of indigenous grapes, across a number of regions. Together they are working with over 350 separate small plots, totalling 80 hectares and 43 different varieties of native grapes.

wines.title: AUS Bruant Nature Reserva Cava
wines.header: AUS Bruant Nature Reserva Cava, Catelonia, Spain, 2021
description: Grape: Pansa Blanca (Xarel·lo)

Discover the finesse of this Ancestral cava, distinguished as the first cava crafted without added sulfites. Made from carefully selected organic grapes, this cava ensures impeccable health from vineyard to cellar. Undergoing a single fermentation ending in the bottle, it ages on the lees for a minimum of 15 months before disgorging. Released to the market without dosage, it maintains a pure expression. Enjoy its pale yellow color and fine bubbles, while its bouquet offers floral notes, white fruits such as pear and green apple, and hints of burlap and hazelnuts. On the palate, experience a light and refreshing sensation with integrated and persistent bubbles, accompanied by delicate flavors of white fruit and almonds. Experience the purity and authenticity of this sulfite-free Ancestral cava.
wines.pairing: white fish, shellfish and in particular oysters

description: 80% Nebbiolo with 20% Croatina.

High up in the Alto-Piemonte, and just seven miles from the Swiss border, is the Val d’Ossola where Nebbiolo is known as Prunent. Munaloss is 80% Nebbiolo and 20% Croatina and it’s a fresh, crunchy, lively red, with cherry and raspberry notes. It’s light, fresh and juicy.

wines.title: Castello di Ama ‘L’Apparita’
wines.header: Castello di Ama ‘L’Apparita’ Toscana I.G.T., Italy, 2017
description: 100% Merlot

L’Apparita is the first of the pure Merlot bottlings produced in Tuscany and has been an icon since its debut in 1985. Harvested from two parcels in the upper part of the Bellavista vineyard, the wine spends about 14 months in new and old barriques. To the eye it’s almost opaque, purple with violet tomes. On the nose it’s intense and exotic, with black and blue berry fruits and walnuts. With a mouthful of dense, richly concentrated fruit and a sublimely succulent finish and hugely deserving of its cult status.
For more on the wine maker click here.
Vinous - Antonio Galloni, September 2020 96+points

“I am immediately struck by the power and concentration of the Castello di Ama 2017 L’Apparita. This is an exuberant and gregarious expression of Merlot that has absorbed every last sunbeam of the hot summer season. On the nose, the wine shows beautiful fullness and generosity that spills richly across the senses. Blackberry syrup and cherry liqueur are followed by smoke, tar, toast and sweet chewing tobacco. You taste that extra density in a similar manner, and the rich concentration of the fruit has consequently shaped a more apparent tannin and a little snap of astringency on the close. My sample bottle does not show a reading of the wine’s alcoholic content, but you feel some heat as well. This edition of L’Apparita is extra dark, succulent and firm. When the wine has been given another five to ten years of cellar age, then I’d suggest guinea fowl or one of those delicious roasted pigeon dishes you find in Tuscany. Some 7,300 bottles were made.”
Wine Advocate, May 2020 96 points.

“Intense and exotic on the nose with blackberry, blueberry, violet and walnut aromas that follow through to a full body with layers of ripe tannins and a beautiful finish of polished and well poised fruit. It goes on and on. I am impressed by the freshness here, as well as the intensity for the vintage. Drink in 2023 and onwards, but a joy to taste now.”
jamessuckling.com, July, 2020 97 points.
wines.pairing: red meat, game and aged hard cheese

quote.text: The 2017 L’Apparita, Ama’s 100% Merlot, is silky, polished and exceptionally beautiful. In 2017, L’Apparita is restrained and elegant more than it is powerful. I have seen L’Apparita blossom with a few years in bottle. I imagine it will be the case here too. Today, L’Apparita is decidedly nuanced and elegant.

wines.title: Castello di Ama ‘Vigneto Bellavista’ Chianti Classico
wines.header: Castello di Ama ‘Vigneto Bellavista’ Chianti Classico Gran Selezione, Italy, 2018
description: 80% Sangiovese and 20% Malvasia Nera

From a plot of 22 parcels the Bellavista is a blend of 80% Sangiovese and 20% Malvasia Nera. It is a deep ruby-red with an exotic blend of dark berries, pomegranate and tobacco on the nose.  It’s deliciously juicy and succulent, with a seductively silky and supple texture. This is one for the cellar!
For more on the wine maker click here.
Wine Spectator, May 2022 94 Points.

“The 2018 Chianti Classico Gran Selezione Vigneto Bellavista marries Sangiovese and Malvasia Nera, a combination that works so well. The Bellavista is a powerful, vertical wine endowed with explosive and tremendous energy. Like all the top wines, it needs the better part of a decade to show all it’s got. Gravel, smoke, leather, licorice and scorched earth. 2026 – 2041”
Vinous - Antonio Galloni, September 2021 98 points.

“This is a very deep and serious Chianti Classico with bark, dark-mushroom and blackberry aromas that follow through to a full body with very polished and integrated tannins that are long and classy. A sophisticated and glorious wine. Drink in 2024 and onwards, but already very pretty.”
jamessuckling.com, August 2021 97 points.

“Camphor, dark spice, blue flower and a whiff of forest floor shape the alluring nose on this delicious red. Elegantly structured and all about finesse and flavor, the savory, focused palate delivers juicy Marasca cherry, orange zest, licorice and cassis alongside taut, ultrarefined tannins. Made with 80% Sangiovese and 20% Malvasia Nera, it’s beautifully balanced, with bright acidity. 2025–2038”

wines.header: Matallana 2019, Ribera del Duero, Spain
description: Matallana is testament of Telmo Rodriguez and Pablo Egnziza's commitment to making ancestral wines. Wines that are styled on how, and where, the wines were made and how they would have tasted from a region that has being making wines for over 1300 years. The pair started making wine in Ribera del Duero in 1998 and today they work across eleven separate vineyards and across five villages, with the village of Sotillo de la Ribera being the epicenter. (The lines across the label are the names of the 11 villages, blacked out, but that's another story). Rare and abandoned vines were reclaimed, new vines were grafted from these ancestral vines and planted as they would have been, as bush vines. The vines are organic, hand harvested with indigenous yeasts used for fermentation.

"An elegant year and this is how the nose of Matallana shows: famously fine. Black cherry, some charcoal behind, fine mint and eucalyptus trace, but ultra polished. Not at all reminiscent of sweet Ribera. More suggestive of Rioja on the nose. Then comes a mouthfeel that will be hard to beat for straightforwardness. Wow, what an ultra sharp black peppery black cherry definition! The sides are super clearly drawn, you immediately know where up, down, left and right are. The whole thing is accompanied by an extremely stony, salty minerality, black pepper, mint and eucalyptus. So black and at the same time so ultra-fine, so sweet and at the same time full of finesse! With more air the wine also develops red fruit, from sour cherry to raspberry and final even to red currant with that ultimate freshness. For Ribera del Duero, Matallana has its own dimension for me in this voluptuous, full-bodied, soft, ultra-sleek and fresh finesse. Opposites that seem almost incompatible. But the wine is so super polished. This brilliant freshness almost cannot be attributed to the Ribera del Duero region. An intense, super fine finesse blockbuster. The wine is definitely at the top of the region along with some other products, there Dominio del Aguila is definitely not so far! A superb masterpiece!" Heiner Lobenberg 97-100/100

"The 2019 Matallana is a blend of 85% Tinto Fino with some 15% other varieties such as Valenciano (Bobal), Navarro (Garnacha) and even white Albillo. 2019 was a very classical vintage with power, concentration and plenty of tannin, and the wine should develop and benefit from extended time in bottle. The wine feels very young and primary, with integrated spices from the élevage in oak, a medium to full-bodied palate, powerful and concentrated but very balanced. description: "Falcoeira, As Caborcas and O Diviso have helped us to understand the complexity of the region." Telmo Rodriguez

O Diviso forms part of an old, abandoned vineyard just outside of the small town of As Ermitas and it’s one of Telmo’s most treasured sites. On steep north facing slopes, over 700 meters in altitude, which have been partially encroached by chestnut trees over the decades. Currently there is 1.2ha of old vines of mencía, garnacha, merenzao, mouratón, and caíño tinto. Minimum intervention, wild yeast fermentation of handpicked, organic grapes. There’s limited availability with only 790 bottles which were bottled in July 2022 from one single 600-liter barrel.

"Wines from O Diviso are ultra-ethereal and graceful, with great tension and subtlety. O Diviso is refined and serious, with the finesse and length that only the world’s greatest vineyards are capable of." De Maison Selections

"A lovely, fresh red with lots of herbs, stems, sauerkraut and white pepper. Excellent depth of wild berries with decadent roses. Really juicy and fresh on the palate with a medium body and firm tannins. A little more firmness and verticality here than the Falcoeira and As Caborcas." James Suckling. Drink now. 95/100

"The superb 2020 O Diviso comes from a warm and healthy vintage when they harvested the grapes quite early but with very balanced ripeness. They picked the grapes the 24th of September. It was the last plot to be harvested (always the last), but the bottled wine has only 13% alcohol. It comes through as aromatic, serious, elegant and balanced, reflecting a cooler place that even in a warmer year ripens slowly. It did ripen well this year and developed a full array of aromas and flavors, giving it complexity and depth and a fine-boned palate. It's one of the finest vintages of O Diviso and my favorite red in 2020. 790 bottles were filled in July 2022 from one single 600-liter barrel." Robert Parker 97/100

"The nose is highly charming, running full on red fruit. Although the percentage of Garnacha is so small, the varietal is still right up front on the nose with a sweet raspberry-strawberry jam. Still, the wine is not heavy, just incredibly fine, charming and sweet. The mouth is much more focused in contrast, staying much leaner with red crisp, red currant, a bit of sour cherry and a bit of raspberry, but in this case not sweet at all. The strawberry is not sweet either. The wine shows more of a lean, focused straightforwardness in the mouth at all, which is very surprising. Cleanly defined left and right, juicy and brilliantly drinkable. Salty on the edges of the tongue. More reminiscent of limestone despite 100% granite soils. A superb beam of red slender fruit, full of finesse and delicacy. To maintain this incredible finesse of the vintage, which is so ripe after all, is already great cinema. Very, very chic! Heiner Lobenberg 97-98/100

To many, Telmo Rodriguez, who, along with his sister Amaia, runs the impressive Remelluri winery in Rioja, needs no introduction but it's his partnership with fellow winemaker, Pablo Egnziza that has created the exciting range of wines that come together under the umbrella of Telmo Rodriguez Wines. The two have have spent the past thirty years reclaiming abandoned vineyards of indigenous grapes, across a number of regions. Together they are working with over 350 separate small plots, totalling 80 hectares and 43 different varieties of native grapes.

wines.title: Ottin 'Non Expedit' Syrah 2023
wines.header: Ottin 'Non Expedit' Syrah, Vallée d'Aoste, Italy, 2023
description: 100% Syrah

A beautifully expressive high-altitude Syrah from Italy’s tiny Vallée d’Aoste, grown at around 700 metres. Fermented with 25% whole bunches and aged for a year in large French oak, it combines the depth of Syrah with a lovely Alpine freshness and lift.

Soft and aromatic, with violet, rose and spice, followed by savoury notes of black olive, herbs and oregano. Fresh and elegant rather than heavy, with plenty of structure, depth and a long, balanced finish.Pairs well with roast or grilled meats, game, hearty stews and aged cheeses.

wines.title: Pedraneira, Albariño
wines.header: Pedraneira Albariño, Val Do Salnes, Rias Baixas, Spain 2024
description: We've been longtime fans of Eulogio Pomares' Zarate wines so it was an easy decision to add his Pedraneira Albarinos, which come from the most coastal plot within the Francon vineyard. The roots of some the vines are actually directly in contact with the sea and it shows. On the nose you can smell the sea, the crab shells, the seaweed, the ebbing tide, you just know it's going to be saline and minerally. It’s definitely saline and salty and moreish, as you might expect, but with beautifully crystalline citrus and nectarine fruit to balance. The wine spends 6 months on its lees which balances the acidity and salinity beautifully.
This is fantastic Albarino & worth decanting and taking your time with.
There's is never too much of Eulogio's wines to go around so grab some and then get a bit more while you're at it, it will aged nicely!
wines.pairing: white meat, seafood and shellfish

wines.title: Rocca di Montegrossi ‘San Marcellino’ Chianti Classico, DOCG
wines.header: Rocca di Montegrossi ‘San Marcellino’ 2016 Chianti Classico Gran Selezione DOCG, Italy
description: 95% Sangiovese, 5% Pugbitello.

Rocca di Montegrossi is steeped in history, dating back as far as the 7th Century and family of Marco Ricasoli, the winery’s owner, played a central role in the creation of the Chianti region and of Chianti Classico.

Needless to say, they only produce their Gran Selezione from their best grapes and in the greatest of vintages, of wine 2016 was definitely one. The winey has been organic since 2006 and they harvest by hand. There’s a small helping of Pugbitello, about 5%, which is an old Tuscan grape variety. The wines spends 24 months in barrel and another in bottle. It’s bottled unfitered.
This is a phenomenal opportunity to get your hands on some truly excellent Chianti, one that will give you another decade of pleasure.
wines.pairing: Pairs well steak and other red meats

quote.text: Vigna San Marcellino is both youthfully fresh and maturely complex. It includes a healthy dose of the deeply coloured Pugnitello grape, and both this and the Sangiovese saw long post-fermentation macerations of over 30 days in 2016. Liquorice, tarragon and broom interlace with exuberant plum and understated toasted nuances that are seductive. Laden with black cherry and rich, velvety tannins, the palate is creamy in texture, while underlying chalkiness and saline minerality lend energy, leading to a sappy, refreshing finish.

wines.title: San Vito ‘Colle dei Mandorli’ Merlot
wines.header: San Vito ‘Colle dei Mandorli’ Merlot 2019 IGT Toscana, Tuscany, Italy
description: 100% Merlot.

San Vito have been organic since 1982 and they hand harvest their best grapes for their Merlot bottling, the Colle dei Mandorli, meaning Almond Hill. The wine is deep ruby red with a generous, complex nose of pungent spice and ripe red berry. It’s well balanced on the palate, firm-structured yet smooth and opulent, with very fine-grained, fragrant tannins and blueberry fruits.

wines.title: Susana Esteban 'Procura' Tinto
wines.header: Susana Esteban 'Procura' Tinto, Serra de São Mamde, Vinho Regional Alentejano 2017
description: Traditional varieties from São Mamede

One of the hallmarks of Susana's wines are that the grapes are old vine, indigenous and in most cases field blends. Field blends are usually found in once forgotten vineyards where native verities have naturally flourished but their true identity has been lost in time. Where the wine maker has the courage to work with what mother nature has provided them the identity of each vine isn't always the first priority. The Procura (which translates as search or quest) is a perfect example of what can be achieved with what nature has gifted you.

Serra de São Mamede is in the mountains of Portalalegre in the coolest subregion of Alentejo/Alentejano. It's surrounded by the forests of a national park and 700 meters above the plains of Alentejo, as a result Susana's style of wines are 'not' typical of Alentejo, they're fresher by design, more complex and with an elegance that surprises.
wines.pairing: steak, veal and charcuterie

quote.text: Two vineyards, one is the same as for the Procura white – the field blend includes both red and white grapes and winegrowers used to blend them all together. It can be savoured neat as a delightful aperitif, seamlessly incorporated into iconic cocktails like the Negroni and Boulevardier, or enjoyed with tonic or soda, accompanied by a slice of orange. Every sip embodies the essence of Valentia.

wines.title: Zarate 'Balado' Albarino
wines.header: Zarate 'Balado' Albarino, Val Do Salnes, Spain, 2022
description: From two plots within a single, walled in vineyard of extremely old, ungrafted vines. Fermented with indigenous yeasts plus six months aging on its lees the 2019 vintage has a intriguing nose of dried apricot, peach, lemon and apple plus granite minerality. There’s a tempting hint of the lees, dried flowers and white blossom too. On the palate the wine is pure, full-bodied and very mineral in personality, with a great core of tropical fruit balanced by lifting acidity, grip and a very long, rewarding finish. The 2019 Balado is delicious and inviting now but definitely worth sometime in the cellar to show what it’s really capable of. Up to 20 years.
wines.pairing: white meat and seafood. Also a great appetiser

wines.title: Zarate 'El Palomar' Albarino
wines.header: Zarate 'El Palomar' Albarino, Val Do Salnes, Spain, 2019
description: The El Palomar (Dovecote) grapes were planted circa 1850 and are ungrafted pre-phyloxera. It’s the oldest of the 40 small parcels that Zarate farms and one of the oldest vineyards in Rias Bias. The El Palomar is the only one of their whites that sees any wood being fermented in 2200 litre, 15 year old, oak foudre, that gives a more lushish mouthfeel while retaining the family’s signature salty minerality. There’s a seriousness to this wine, due to the incredible age of the vines, with striking complexity and depth.
wines.pairing: white meat, seafood and in particular, shellfish

wines.title: Zarate 'Tras da Vina' Albarino
wines.header: Zarate 'Tras da Vina', Albarino, Val do Salnes, Spain, 20121
description: The Tras da Viña is from a single vineyard, planted from cuttings taken from one of Eulogio’s pre-phylloxera El Palomar vineyard. With up to 24 months on its lees this is a wine of considerable depth and character that offers up a focused aroma of citrus fruits with a defined minerality. This is a full-bodied and complex wine that’s full of life. It’s that bit softer that the Balado so accessible sooner in it’s life but it too is worth sticking aside, at least a few bottles, for another 5-20 years.
wines.pairing: white meat, seafood and shellfish

wines.title: Zarate Albarino Val do Salnes
wines.header: Zarate, Albarino, Val do Salnes, Spain, 2025
description: It’s fair to say that Zarate’s wines have little in common with much of what passes for Albarino these days. Where some commercial styles of Albarino can seem overly ripe and tropical, the wines from Zarate are just the opposite – precise, mineral, and taut, drawing on the salty character of the Atlantic coast to give the wines a remarkable freshness. 2024 is benchmark Zarate, with structure and acidity and this “entry-level” Zarate is crisp, characterful and rewarding with a long, tasty finish, vibrant and almost salty
